newsitem.title: GERMANY: UK's Clarke says stg moves steadied British growth.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke says stg moves steadied British growth.

text.p: British Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke, boasting one of the most robust economies in the Group of Seven (G7) nations, said on Saturday movements in the pound had steadied British economic growth.

"We are at the moment, one of the strongest economies of the G7, with one of the healthiest recoveries underway," Clarke said following a one-day G7 meeting of finance ministers and central bank governors.

"Our labour market works very well so, we've had falling unemployment. Obviously, the change of the exchange rate of the pound has steadied that growth," Clarke said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television, to be broadcast later.
But he said he did not expect sterling's moves to harm the economy.
Clarke added that problems in continental European economies, such as high unemployment, were not due to exchange rate levels.

"If you look across the continent of Europe, the major problem of unemployment, it isn't principally a question of currency allignments. It's wrong to concentrate on things like the value vis-a-vis the dollar," he said.
"The real cause of high unemployment in western Europe, on the continent, is rigidities in the labour market in particular," Clarke said.

"I think the governments of the continent know perfectly well they haven't tackled the question of making their labour markets more flexible and other structural changes in their economies to assure that as their economy does strengthen, it's actually job-creating growth.
